title: GPU-accelerated path-dependent marginal gain
description: Ongoing work evaluates the additional space each viewpoint contributes along a candidate exploration path.
introduction: Successive viewpoints along a path often observe overlapping parts of a map. This research studies path-dependent marginal gain: crediting each viewpoint only for the additional space that earlier viewpoints on the same candidate path are not already expected to reveal.

problem.heading: Count newly observed space once.
paragraphs: Scoring every viewpoint independently can give repeated credit to the same unknown region. A path containing several overlapping views may then appear more informative than the new space it would actually reveal.

Accounting for those overlaps makes path evaluation more demanding. The research asks how to retain the history of expected observations while keeping the overlap calculation suitable for onboard planning.

approach.heading: Use the path’s observation history.
paragraphs: The method represents earlier viewpoints along a candidate path using compact depth-buffer histories. These histories describe which regions are already expected to be visible before a new candidate view is evaluated.
GPU-parallel overlap tests compare candidate observations against that accumulated history. The resulting marginal-gain score focuses on additional space along the path.

steps.title: Retain earlier views
steps.text: Keep a compact history of observations expected along the candidate path.

steps.title: Check overlap
steps.text: Use parallel tests to identify space covered by earlier viewpoints.

steps.title: Score additional space
steps.text: Credit the candidate view for its new contribution.

evidence.label: Method development
evidence.text: The current research direction explores GPU-accelerated evaluation of path-dependent information gain for onboard exploration planning.

evidence.label: Overlap illustration
evidence.text: The diagram explains how successive viewpoints can share visible regions and why those regions should receive credit only once along a candidate path.
